Subject: Helio: order form — payment split & EU reverse-charge evidence

Hi Priya — thanks again for the time earlier. I’m attaching the latest Order Form (Helio_OrderForm_v3.pdf) with the pricing ladder and proposed minimum commits. Two quick asks so we can get this over to Legal and Procurement: 

1) Payment routing: you mentioned Helio wants the activation fee invoiced to Helio Ltd (UK entity) and the recurring monthly invoices to Helio EU BV (NL). Can you confirm the legal entity names, billing addresses, and preferred PO numbers for each? We’ll reflect this in the order form and in the invoice recipient fields.

2) EU VAT reverse-charge evidence: because Helio EU BV is VAT-registered, we need the VAT registration number + either the vendor confirmation or a tax residency certificate for reverse-charge treatment. If you can upload a short certificate (a scanned VAT certificate or a signed vendor attestation), that will let our billing team mark invoices without VAT. I’ve included Helio_TaxResidencyCertificate.pdf as a placeholder if you already have it.

I’ve cc’d Kimberly and Karthik — Kimberly, can Legal confirm whether we need any extra contract language in the Order Form appendix to reflect multi-entity invoicing and the reverse-charge process? Karthik — for accounting: will Redwood split the invoice streams in our system or create consolidated invoices with internal splits?

Next steps: if you can share the entity details and attach the VAT evidence, we’ll update the order form, push it to DocuSign, and include the PO mapping on the first page.

Thanks —
Alex Martinez
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Helio_OrderForm_v3.pdf (application/pdf, 238 KB)]

Recurring: Helio EU BV (NL) — Helio EU BV, Prins Hendrikkade 100, 1012 Amsterdam, NL — PO HL-EU-SUB-2027.

Subject: Fwd: Helio: order form — payment split & EU reverse-charge evidence

Kimberly / Karthik — forwarding Priya’s confirmation and the tax certificate. Key items for Legal / Billing: 

- We need an explicit mapping in the Order Form: Activation fee -> Helio Ltd (UK) + PO HL-UK-ACT-2027; Recurring subscriptions -> Helio EU BV (NL) + PO HL-EU-SUB-2027.
- Helio confirmed they want separate invoices per entity (not a consolidated invoice) — Redwood needs to issue distinct documents and route collections accordingly.
- Tax evidence is attached (Helio_TaxResidencyCertificate.pdf). If Legal is comfortable, we’ll mark recurring invoices as reverse-charge exempt. Please confirm the exact language to add to the appendix for invoice recipient and VAT handling (suggestion below).

Suggested appendix language (draft):
"Billing and Tax Treatment: Redwood will issue separate invoices to the invoicing entities listed on the signature page. For invoices to Helio EU BV (NL), Redwood will apply the EU reverse-charge mechanism provided Helio supplies a valid VAT registration number and supporting residency documentation prior to the first invoice. If supporting documentation is not provided, Redwood reserves the right to invoice VAT to the recipient entity."

Kimberly — any redline suggestions to tighten allocation of liability on VAT misclassification? Karthik — how quick can Billing create two invoice recipients in our ERP and ensure separate AR aging?

I’ll wait for your edits, then we’ll push to DocuSign and include the HubSpot deal link.

Best,
Alex
[Forwarded attachment: Helio_TaxResidencyCertificate.pdf]

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Helio: order form — payment split & EU reverse-charge evidence

Thanks Alex — high level: I like the suggested appendix language, but two edits: 

1) Add an explicit customer responsibility clause: Helio must provide valid VAT registration information and any supporting government-issued documentation within 10 business days of countersignature; failure to do so will render Redwood entitled to charge applicable VAT to the invoiced entity and to recover any tax, interest or penalties.

2) Add a short mechanics bullet clarifying that separate invoices will each carry their own invoice number, payment terms, and potential late fee assessments (do not conflate payment terms across entities).

I don’t think we need additional liability carve-outs beyond the above, but I’ll mark the redlines and return an annotated order form by EOD tomorrow. Karthik — once legal posts the redline, let’s confirm AR mapping (two recipients) and whether we need two separate payment instructions on page 1.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
[Will upload marked Order Form (annotated) to HubSpot and link back to deal]
